title: The Far Summit
premise: Ansel Thornbury, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vane brothers' salvage syndicate, discovers a tide-revealed cave on the Far Summit coast containing the wreck of the Meridian Star and its rumored cargo of colonial gold. Racing the fleet by six tides before monsoon landfall, she must decide whether to sell out the cave's guardian community—who have hidden the wreck for generations—to clear her debt, or expose the truth that could destroy them all. Betrayed by her own borrowed identity as a surveyor, Ansel learns the debt was a trap designed to flush out the wreck's location. In the end she outruns neither the storm nor the fleet but turns both against each other, sinking the evidence and herself into a new name among the people she once planned to rob.
about_author: O. M. Yarrow is the pen name of a former maritime cartographer who spent a decade charting monsoon coastlines before turning to fiction. They write from a houseboat that has been 'nearly seaworthy' for six years.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Chasing a storm along the Far Summit coast to film footage she can sell, Ansel counts down her debt deadline with the Vane brothers while cataloguing what little she owns: a compass, a camera, and a forged surveyor's license. The chapter establishes her invisibility as survival strategy. Emotional beat: weary defiance masking dread.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. An extreme low tide exposes a sea cave beneath the cliffs; inside, she finds timbers stamped with the Meridian Star's mark and carvings suggesting the wreck was deliberately hidden. She photographs everything, already calculating the payout. Emotional beat: greed and wonder arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Optimists
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, with an interlude letter from creditor Dree Vane. Ansel reports a 'promising lead' without specifics, buying time, but Dree's warm reply reveals the Vanes know more about the Meridian Star than they should—and that her debt was never meant to be repaid in money. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of her plan.

chapters.title: The Keepers of Salt Hollow
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Investigating the cave's carvings leads her to Salt Hollow, a fishing village whose elders have guarded the wreck for generations, believing its cargo cursed. Posing as a surveyor, she befriends ferryman Ilo Kestrel, who recognizes her compass as one lost with the Meridian's last keeper. Emotional beat: belonging she didn't ask for.

chapters.title: Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Ilo's POV. Ilo suspects Ansel is lying but shows her the village archive anyway, revealing the wreck carried not just gold but documents proving the Vanes' founding fortune was stolen from Salt Hollow's ancestors. Ilo chooses to trust her, and hates himself for it. Emotional beat: loyalty extended on faith.

chapters.title: Two Tides Gone
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The Vanes' salvage fleet appears on the horizon—someone sold the cave's location. Ansel realizes her own photographs were traced, and that confessing to Ilo means losing the only person who trusts her. She stays silent and helps the village prepare defenses instead. Emotional beat: guilt calcifying into resolve.

chapters.title: The Price of the Hold
chapters.summary: Dree Vane's POV. Aboard the flagship, Dree offers Ansel full debt forgiveness for the cave's exact coordinates, revealing she knows Ansel's real name and the crime that made her flee to the coast. Ansel accepts the meeting as cover—but Dree sees through it. Emotional beat: power wielded like weather, patient and total.

chapters.title: Monsoon Landfall
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The storm hits early; the fleet anchors in the bay to wait it out, trapping everyone. Ansel confesses everything to Ilo—the debt, the false name, the photographs—and offers the only plan left: use her storm-chasing rig to lure the fleet onto the shoals during peak surge. Emotional beat: truth offered at the worst possible moment, and accepted.

chapters.title: The Wrecking Light
chapters.summary: Alternating Ansel and Ilo POVs. During the surge, Ansel runs the false beacon from the cliff while Ilo guides villagers to cut the fleet's anchor lines. The flagship grounds on the shoals; Dree, refusing rescue until the gold is secured, goes down with her ambition. The cave floods, sealing the wreck forever. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: A New Name Among Strangers
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Aftermath: the Vanes' syndicate collapses without its flagship, Ansel's debt drowned with it. The village offers her Ilo's grandfather's compass back—not as proof of blood, but as invitation. She takes a new name, keeps the old one stitched inside her coat, and stays through the first calm morning. Emotional beat: identity chosen rather than escaped.
